text: Although both cultures observe the same cycle of light and darkness, they may organize time around different activities, beliefs, and environmental conditions. A farming community might distinguish periods for milking, fieldwork, and resting, while another culture might emphasize prayer times, communal meals, or trading hours. Seasonal changes and local climate can also influence which parts of the day matter most. Thus, meaningful divisions of time reflect not only natural patterns but also the social priorities and shared traditions through which people interpret them.
